alignments.note: Finite verb with its supplied subject, discontinuous under rule 15; head on the lexical verb (rule 9).

γαμίζω rendered *are given in marriage*. Rule 91's operational test puts the head on the word the corpus spends on the lexeme: the γαμ- family is spent on *marry* and *marriage* — γαμοῦσιν → *marry* in this same verse, γάμος → *marriage*/*wedding* at 22:2, 22:3, 22:4, 22:8, 22:9 and 22:10 — and never on *give*, which the corpus spends on δίδωμι (22:17). *given* is the phrase's formal English verb head, which rule 17 forbids choosing for that reason alone, so the head is *marriage*, as *make known* heads on *known* and *bear witness* on *witness*. Heading on *given* under rule 9's plain-passive reading remains defensible and is the reading this unit previously carried.
Comparative adverb; no correlative καί stands, so rules 82 and 100 are not in question.
The ASV gives *heaven* no determiner, so the article has nothing to anchor (rules 21, 23).

review_notes: Corrected the target head of s008 from *given* to *marriage* under rule 91: the corpus spends the γαμ- root family on *marry* and *marriage*, never on *give*, and *given* could only have been chosen as the English phrase's formal verb head, which rule 17 refuses.
Variant v019 covers no source token; nothing to align for it.
Edges are unchanged throughout; the ASV's *in* inside *given in marriage* answers to no Greek preposition and stays inside the verb's unit.
